objective_pt: Recognise and use understatement, sarcasm and self-deprecating humour ("Well, that went well", "It's not the end of the world"), and react naturally when someone is joking.

teacher.goal_pt: Compare Brazilian and English-speaking humour, especially British understatement.
prompts: Is Brazilian humour more direct or more ironic?
Has anyone ever misunderstood one of your jokes in English?
watchFor: "Joke" vs "kid": "Are you kidding?" is the natural form, not "Are you joking with me?".

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat with an ironic, flat tone, as if something has just gone wrong.
It's pouring with rain and your friend says "Lovely weather for a picnic." What does she mean?
options: She wants to have a picnic.
She's being sarcastic: the weather is terrible.
She thinks the rain is lovely.
exercises.explanation_pt: Sarcasm says the opposite of what is meant, often with a flat or exaggerated tone.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Você está brincando!"

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Brincar" in the sense of joking is "kid" or "joke". "You're playing" means you're playing a game.
"Brincando comigo" is "kidding me" / "pulling my leg", not "joking with me".

teacher.goal_pt: Humour vocabulary: tongue-in-cheek, deadpan, understatement, to pull someone's leg, self-deprecating.
prompts: Do you know anyone with a deadpan sense of humour?
When did someone last pull your leg?
watchFor: "Humor" stressed as in Portuguese (hu-MOR) instead of HU-mour.
"Funny" vs "fun": a funny person makes you laugh; a fun person is enjoyable to be with.

exercises.meaning_pt: zoar alguém, fazer alguém de bobo (de brincadeira)
exercises.example_en: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg.

exercises.meaning_pt: sem expressão, com cara séria (ao fazer piada)
exercises.example_en: She has a brilliant deadpan delivery.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.pt: eufemismo, dizer menos do que é

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Relaxa, eu só estou te zoando."
accepted: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg
Relax, I'm just messing with you
Don't worry, I'm just pulling your leg

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Zoar" is "kid", "tease" or "pull someone's leg". "Play with you" sounds childish or odd.
commonErrors.correction_en: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The idiom is "pull someone's leg", with "leg", not "foot".
commonErrors.correction_en: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg.

teacher.goal_pt: Intonation of sarcasm: flat or exaggerated pitch, lengthened vowels.
prompts: Say "Oh, brilliant" as if your train was just cancelled.
watchFor: Same tone for sincere and sarcastic versions, so the irony is lost.
Overacting so much that it sounds aggressive.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat sarcastically: stretch "brilliant" and keep the pitch low and flat.
exercises.prompt: Oh, brilliant. Just what I needed.
accepted: Oh, brilliant. Just what I needed

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat this understatement in a calm, dry voice.
exercises.prompt: It's not exactly the best idea I've ever heard.
accepted: It's not exactly the best idea I've ever heard
It is not exactly the best idea I have ever heard

exercises.explanation_pt: In English the stress is on the first syllable: HU-mour (/ˈhjuː.mər/), unlike "humor" in Portuguese.

teacher.goal_pt: Detect irony from context and tone, and play along.
prompts: How could you reply with a joke?
watchFor: Literal answers to jokes ("No, the weather is bad").
Missing understatement ("a bit of a problem" = a big problem).

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. How bad is the situation really?
exercises.listen: The car broke down, it started snowing and we missed the wedding. So, yeah, it was a bit of a disappointing day.
options: Actually very bad. The speaker is using understatement.
exercises.explanation_pt: "A bit of a disappointing day" after a list of disasters is classic understatement.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. Your friend is joking about herself. Reply light-heartedly.
exercises.listen: I tried to bake a cake yesterday and I set off the fire alarm. Twice.
accepted: Well, at least you know the alarm works!
Remind me never to eat your cake!
That sounds like my kind of cooking!

commonErrors.explanation_pt: She's joking about herself, so a serious apology misses the tone. Play along: "At least the alarm works!"
commonErrors.correction_en: Well, at least you know the alarm works!

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and reply with an understatement about the weather.
exercises.listen: Have you seen it outside? It's like a hurricane out there.
accepted: It's a bit windy, isn't it?
Not exactly beach weather, is it?
Yes, it's a bit wild out there

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The Portuguese "né?" becomes a question tag in English: "It's a bit windy, isn't it?", not "windy, no?".
commonErrors.correction_en: It's a bit windy, isn't it?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: That's accurate, but the task asks for understatement: say less than it is ("a bit windy").
commonErrors.correction_en: It's a bit windy, isn't it?

teacher.goal_pt: Tell a funny story using self-deprecation and understatement; react to the teacher's irony.
prompts: Tell me about your worst cooking (or DIY) disaster.
(Teacher uses sarcasm.) Did you get it?
What kind of jokes don't translate well from Portuguese?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Não sou exatamente o melhor motorista do mundo."
accepted: I'm not exactly the best driver in the world
I'm not exactly the world's best driver
I'm not exactly a great driver
I'm not the best driver in the world, to be honest
Let's just say I'm not the best driver in the world
I'm not exactly the best driver ever

commonErrors.explanation_pt: With superlatives and places, English uses "in": "the best driver in the world".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm not exactly the best driver in the world.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Motorist" exists but is formal (news reports). In conversation, "motorista" is "driver".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm not exactly the best driver in the world.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Não é o fim do mundo."
accepted: It's not the end of the world
It isn't the end of the world
That's not the end of the world
It's hardly the end of the world
Well, it's not the end of the world

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Keep both articles: "the end of the world".
commonErrors.correction_en: It's not the end of the world.

exercises.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to make a self-deprecating joke.
accepted: Let's just say cooking isn't my strong point

exercises.instruction_pt: Tell a short funny story about yourself in about a minute, using understatement or self-deprecation.
exercises.prompt_en: Tell me about a time when something went hilariously wrong for you. Don't be afraid to laugh at yourself.
guidelines_pt: Use self-deprecation: "Let's just say I'm not the most...".
Use understatement for the worst moment: "It was a bit of a disaster."
End with a punchline or "Well, at least...".

teacher.goal_pt: Recycle humour vocabulary and check the learner can switch between literal and ironic readings.
prompts: Say something sarcastic about Monday mornings.
watchFor: Flat intonation that hides the irony.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Ele tem um senso de humor muito seco."
accepted: He has a very dry sense of humour
He has a very dry sense of humor
He's got a very dry sense of humour
He's got a really dry sense of humor
He has a really dry sense of humour
His sense of humour is very dry

commonErrors.correction_en: He has a very dry sense of humour.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Adjectives go before the noun: "a very dry sense of humour".
commonErrors.correction_en: He has a very dry sense of humour.

exercises.sentence: Don't take it seriously, I'm only pulling your ___.

commonErrors.correction_en: Don't take it seriously, I'm only pulling your leg.

options: This is the worst day of my entire life!
Losing my wallet was slightly inconvenient.
I'm so happy I could fly!
exercises.explanation_pt: Understatement makes something sound less serious than it is: "slightly inconvenient" for a lost wallet.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat with a smile in your voice.
exercises.prompt: Well, it could have been worse.
accepted: Well, it could have been worse
